senses.gloss: (of a woman betrothed in childhood, on arriving at majority) to protest against, to annul one’s marriage.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 13:1">Yeb. XIII, 1</cite> <he>אין מְמָאֲנִין אלא ארוסות</he> only betrothed (not married) women may have their obligation cancelled.

<cite ref="Mishnah Yevamot 13:1">Ib.</cite> <he>מְמָאֶנֶת והיא קטנה וכ׳</he> she may protest (have her marriage cancelled) even while yet a minor, and even four or five times in succession. Ib. 2 <he>איזו … שצריכה למָאֵן</he> what minor is bound to make declaration (before leaving her husband)?—Ib. 4 <he>הממאנת באיש וכ׳</he> if a woman refuses her husband by declaration, he is permitted to marry her kindred (who otherwise would be forbidden to him); a. v. fr.

<cite ref="Mishnah Eduyot 6:1">Eduy. VI, 1</cite> <he>שמְמָאֲנִים וכ׳</he> that the court eventually advises women married as minors to protest; <cite ref="Niddah 8a:35">Nidd. 8ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Berakhot 27a:9">Ber. 27ᵃ</cite>.—V. <cite ref="M01077"><he>מִיאוּן</he></cite>.

senses.gloss: מֵיאֵן, מֵאֵן (b. h.; v. אֵין) to deny, refuse, esp.
